requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named “OS Comparison Root CA” on node1.
requirements.summary: The final self-signed certificate has the requested subject and issuer, critical CA and signing extensions, and a matching root-owned private key with mode 600. It also successfully issued test leaf certificates before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Install its certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1.
requirements.summary: The certificate matches the installed anchor, appears as a p11-kit trust anchor, validates through RHEL’s system CA bundle, and enables system-bundle verification of issued leaf certificates. These results persisted after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The provider restart protocol is also strong: it records pre-restart identity and working CA/trust state, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, a running system with no failed units, persisted key/certificate/anchor data, and successful post-restart issuance and trust verification. Fixed boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inspect certificate or trust-store contents, so their independent cross-check covers reboot and general node health; CA persistence is established by captured executor commands.
The trace contains an initially defective certificate installation, but coherent final and post-restart observations demonstrate that it was replaced successfully.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or retained residue was observed. The only avoidable mutation was prematurely installing and extracting the first certificate into system trust before validating it (cmd-6abf6cbfa5574805); subsequent evidence showed that version was unverifiable (cmd-af13335d711244f1). It was fully replaced by the corrected certificate (cmd-cd3ec0aa527549af) and did not remain. Temporary proof files were bounded and cleaned, the protocol-required reboot left no failed units or new exposure, and package health remained intact.
